title: 911 death inquest recommends changes
article: A coroner's jury looking into the death of a woman from Casselman recommends that one agency oversee the province's current patchwork of 911 service.

Kathryn Missen, 54, died during an asthma attack at her home in Casselman. She called 911 but was unable to speak. An OPP officer wasn't dispatched to Missen's home until 90 minutes later; the officer forgot about the call during a busy shift, and never actually went to the scene.
Missen was found dead two days later, when neighbours became worried that they had not seen her.
The coroner's jury made 27 recommendations, Thursday, following a three-week inquest into Missen's death, as well as those of three other people, near Sudbury.
Many of the recommendations are highly technical, including that all emergency services should use compatible dispatch systems by 2023.
The jury also wants staff in the 911 centre to be alerted if there's a delay in dispatching help to an emergency.
